answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether inspecting a bridge or identifying antique ivory. Each additional identity needs its own bond, so a tide of 10,000 fake agents ties up $1 million. The attacker can still create accounts, but cannot cheaply turn them into active sellers: scaling the swarm requires proportional capital and sacrifices its use elsewhere for a month.
